# dsh-relaycheck
A DeepSeek Harness plugin that gives the agent a `relay_check` tool: ask it "is this relay really se
rving the model it claims?" and it runs relaycheck against the relay and reports a verdict.
中文：给 dsh 的 agent 加一个 `relay_check` 工具，用 relaycheck 检测 LLM API 中转是否货真价实（模型是否被调包、计费是否虚报、上下文是否被截断、是否注入隐
sh 的 agent 加一个 `relay_check` 工具，用 relaycheck 检测 LLM API 中转是否货真价实（模型是否被调包、计费是否虚报、上下文是否被截断、是否注入隐藏提示词）。
## What it checks
relaycheck runs four groups against the relay and compares the answers with a reference fingerprint:
| Group | What it catches |
| identity | model swap: 24 probes × N samples, permutation χ² per probe, Cauchy-combined p-value |

| protocol | wrong or missing protocol fields for the claimed API |
| billing | reported `usage` vs.

the real token count; hidden prompt injection |
| context | truncated context window (needle test)

the real token count; hidden prompt injection |
| context | truncated context window (needle test) |
The verdict is `consistent`, `inconsistent` or `inconclusive`. It is a statistical test, not proof.

## Configure
The model can only name a **configured target**. Base URLs and key variable names live in your profi
le config, so a prompt injection cannot point your key at another host. Keys are read from environme
ompt injection cannot point your key at another host. Keys are read from environment variables only.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Each `baseUrl` must be an `http://` or `https://` URL and each `keyEnv` a plain variable name (`[A-Z
a-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`); the tool checks both, and that the variable is set and non-empty, before it st
arts relaycheck, so a misconfigured target costs no tokens.
When `provider` matches the provider of the current session, the agent can call `relay_check` with n
o arguments to test "the relay I'm using now", with the session's model.
| Option | Default | Meaning |

| `targets` | `{}` | named relays the agent may check |
| `defaultTarget` | — | used when the call n

ames none and no provider matches |
| `samples` | `16` | samples per identity probe |
| `probes` | `

identity,protocol,billing,context` | groups to run |
| `allowDeep` | `false` | let the agent request

`--deep` |
| `requireApproval` | `true` | approval prompt before every run |
| `lang` | `en` | `en`

or `zh` for the summaries |
| `timeoutSeconds` | `600` | kill the run after this long (the tool the
n reports a timeout) |
## The tool
`relay_check({ target?, model?, probes?, deep? })` returns:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`pValue` and `injectedTokens` are left out when relaycheck reports none. The model sees a short text
summary of the same facts.
The key is passed to relaycheck by variable name only, never on the command line. relaycheck redacts
it from its own output; the plugin additionally replaces any occurrence of the key's exact value wi
th `***` in the result and in error messages, as a second line of defence.
When a run fails, the tool returns an ordinary error the model can read instead of a result:
- relaycheck exits without a report (unreachable relay, HTTP errors, non-JSON responses, bad argumen

ts): `relaycheck failed (exit N): <last lines of relaycheck's stderr>`
- the run hits `timeoutSecond

s`: `relaycheck timed out after Ns`
- the report has no valid `verdict` (for example an incompatible
relaycheck version): the tool says so rather than returning a partial result
Cancelling the tool call, or disposing the plugin (profile reload, dsh exit), stops a run in progres
ncelling the tool call, or disposing the plugin (profile reload, dsh exit), stops a run in progress.
## Cost
A default run sends a few hundred short requests (24 probes × `samples`, plus protocol, billing and
context checks) and takes one to several minutes. That is why `requireApproval` is on by default.
## Development
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The suite covers config validation, target resolution, argv building, malformed reports, key redacti
on, abort/timeout handling and plugin disposal inside a real cordis + dsh-tools context. End-to-end
cases run relaycheck against its own local mock relays (honest, model-swapping, token-injecting) and
against small local HTTP servers that refuse connections, hang, return non-JSON, or echo the key ba
ainst small local HTTP servers that refuse connections, hang, return non-JSON, or echo the key back.
